name: The Hill School - campus reconstruction at 2 blocks per metre

components.name: Athey Academic Center, Dining Hall and connecting court

findings: Narrow glazing centres are visibly more open than baseline and retain their pane texture. Broad outer surrounds remain coarse at two blocks per metre.
Middle-sill blue daylight seen in v1 is closed by original-shape sill haunches and bounded brick backing.
Upper east-return windows respect the existing flat-bay correction and retain complete heads; the nine physically unsupported band cells visible in v3 are absent.
Quad rhythm, source orientation, ground exposure, roof silhouette and the court context are preserved in the six cameras.
limits: The 179 open or mixed conservative ray cases remain unresolved. Inward directions are inferred; these are not 179 confirmed photographic holes and are not proof that every frame is fully enclosed. Future enclosure work needs declared opening planes and connected occupied shapes.
Eighteen partial arch contacts touch real shapes but do not establish every sightline through the curved perimeter. Dark glass or deep interior space was not filled speculatively.
Narrow sash divisions are below the retained half-metre block resolution and are represented by the original gray pane texture. Exact sash counts and minor trim dimensions remain source-limited.
Dining Hall facade, hidden elevations, the west connector enclosure, exact materials and overall photographic likeness remain unresolved.
verdict.scope: Native-verified targeted frame repair accepted as an ongoing campus context study. This is not a complete facade-enclosure, finished-building or photographic-likeness approval.

components.integration_scope: Native-verified bounded Athey frame repair; unresolved enclosure probes remain and Dining Hall is still an envelope.

accepted_findings: All six supplied native views inspected against the campaign photograph and supplied source qualifications.

Campaign, northwest porch and entry views show a continuous shallow brown cover and level cream exterior fascia; the earlier disconnected white ribbons are resolved. Root independently confirms this finding.
Roof view confirms the retained measured main roof, larger central dormer and separately authored smaller western dormer; the main cornice is reduced without exposing the final wall backing.
White-pane sash sheets remain connected and closed at their authorised perimeter; original-model roof occupancy checks independently establish contact across all 376 adjacent porch-cover pairs.
verdict.acceptance_scope: Integrate the individual measured-footprint Meigs v4 study with its qualified northern campaign interpretation and documented bounded porch/small-dormer corrections. This accepts the reviewed construction and visual proxy; unseen elevations and exact photographic registration remain unresolved.

material_decision.decision: Retain verified spruce roof appearance proxy, white terracotta stucco field, quartz trim, narrow pale-oak posts/rails and white stained panes.
material_decision.actual_roof_product: Unresolved: campaign brown overlapping units do not establish wood, asphalt or synthetic composition; the supplied drone shows a grayer appearance.

remaining_limits: The campaign north/west orientation is moderate-confidence positional interpretation, not calibrated registration.
Spruce is warmer and more visibly wood-grained than some supplied aerial roof views; roof product, aging and exposure differences are unresolved.
White terracotta underrepresents stippled buff stucco and retains a modest pink bias.
Quarter-grid roof coping and three necessary full backing positions beside dormer panes remain heavier than the narrow photographed cornice.
Pane mesh has its intrinsic quarter-metre depth at two blocks per metre; original white borders approximate individual sash rails without establishing exact pane counts.
Smaller dormer bounds, post spacing, chimney portions, partial window edges, west doorway and entrance risers are estimates from incomplete imagery and grade.
Pale-oak fence post shafts are narrower than the photographed posts and retain timber-joint texture.
East/south and most west elevations remain unresolved with no mirrored invented window rows; retained low eastern source fragments are not claimed as photographically verified occupied roofs.

components.name: Warner Center for Spiritual Life and Equity

findings: All six fresh native screenshots inspected against official source crops 270 and 272.
Seven distinct masonry gables with thin pale sloped caps replace the full-height white teeth seen in rejected v9.
Pond glazing reads taller; pale front-only jambs and masonry returns expose more glass in oblique views.
Both long walls now follow regular single-plane grid steps without inherited raster buttresses; measured rotation and county placement remain unchanged.
Measured long roof, projecting cross-gable, two-stage open porch, attached posts and four connected pale rails read coherently.
Central door is restored to its v8 X264 reveal; transparent transoms and backed head close the detected contact gap. No visible new daylight slit at the inspected door, pane or roof contacts.
Native report provenance and exact archive-to-Anvil parity pass for all 644,247 occupied blocks.
verdict.acceptance_boundary: Bounded visible exterior improvement over v8/v9, including below-eave west wall regularization. This does not certify photographic completeness, unseen west/south apertures, or the whole campus.
remaining_limitations: Half-metre blocks still make gable and arch profiles chunky and locally asymmetric.
Rotated corners make apparent trim widths uneven in oblique views despite connected planar construction.
West and south opening schedules remain unverified; no west windows are invented.
The east 62 m gable ridges, opening registration, door divisions, post registration, deck grade and rail substrate remain documented interpretations.
Source roof slopes and raster outline retain measured irregularity; no whole-roof smoothing was applied.
Window positions are scaled from drone imagery, with about 1m uncertainty; 1.15m source width quantizes to 1m clear glazing at 2 blocks/m.
Seven east gables and four plain windows are directly observed. West roof projections remain provisional symmetry; west apertures are unresolved and are not mirrored.
56.25m entrance and deck level is a DEM/photo interpretation, not a building survey.
Four pale porch posts are interpreted support locations fitted to the actual retained source canopy and authored outer hood; exact post dimensions and registration remain unmeasured.
Ordinary quartz stairs approximate the round arches and thin fascia; original block shapes impose visible quarter/half-metre steps.
The rail substrate is unresolved; pale oak is Sol's painted-white appearance proxy, not an assertion of real wood species.

verdict.inspection: All six matching original-client native views inspected against the supplied pitch photo and rejected v13 images. The bounded cap-position/perimeter correction is accepted.

screenshots.finding: The corrected end corner sits within the measured wall. Connected narrow end glazing, lower storeys and the real grade are retained.
Wing/centre aperture counts and original brick/gray-roof silhouette remain. The broad v13 white cap bands are removed; glazing reads continuously within the original wall.
The sash centres stay transparent from top to bottom and attach to the masonry frame. Some slender sill pieces remain visible. Rounded portal shoulders and the attic vent remain coarse.
Clear sash centres continue on the rear; the low basement and terraced grade remain. The rear opening schedule is unobserved and remains a proposal.
Main roof intersections, eave backing and the two interpreted stacks are retained. Roof courses and diagonal edges remain strongly stepped at this resolution.
The white-pane rim is visible without former broad opaque inner caps. End opening counts and hidden portions of the front remain source-limited.

verdict.validated_scope: All 793 previous pane cells stay fixed; 249 inner panes replace former opaque caps/backing within the same glazing height. 1,042 panes have zero horizontal/vertical/diagonal-jamb candidates; 4,365 outer/recessed wall cells are nonempty. Source roof values and physical tops remain exact.
remaining_approximations: Half-metre horizontal and quarter-metre vertical grid steps are pronounced at the 34-degree source axis; the footprint and roof are not rotated to hide them.
The rounded portal heads and diamond attic vent are coarser than the photograph.
Some inner sill segments remain visible, and the thin pane texture rim is less uniform than the real painted surrounds.
Rear/end rows, partly hidden pitch counts and chimney geometry remain proposals; native views do not establish unseen source details.
verdict.rejected_baseline: Foster v13; native-review.json records the obstructive white-cap bands that this version removes.

components.name: Rolfe Dormitory - separate triangular portals and stepped rear roof

verdict.inspection: All six original-client native images inspected against existing supplied current drone and historical west-gable reference images.
verdict.bounded_repair_status: Suitable for integration with recorded visual and source uncertainties; not a claim of measured unobserved facades.
observed_improvements: Glass reaches its existing masonry/frame after the bounded inner returns; no new projecting cages or full-height opaque jamb panels.
Distinct closed lower front block, recessed central gable, lower rear hip and steep grade remain intact.
remaining_discrepancies: Some inner white cap blocks remain visible at different raster phases; the photographed white surrounds are more uniform and thinner.
Triangular entrance heads are coarse and shallow at the half-metre horizontal grid.
Small diamond vents read as stepped narrow slots.
Quarter-metre fascia/course steps remain more pronounced than the smooth photographed trim.
Weathered gray roof appearance is approximated by stone-brick textures; lighting differs from the source.
source_limits: Rear, end and basement proposals are not verified by native screenshots.
The six west-gable sashes are historically evidenced; their current state remains uncertain.
Aperture sizes/positions and chimney/flue details are photo estimates.
verdict.structure: See physical-pane-perimeter-audit.json and v5-to-v7-bounded-change-and-backing-audit.json; pair support alone was not used as evidence of closure.

inspected_screenshots.finding: The shuttered brick facade, low end coping, entry hoods and broad dormer retain the reviewed silhouette. No new projecting glass or masonry appears.
Both inspected storeys meet the brick jamb and sill; the added return stays behind the outer pane and shutter face.
The diagonal return is continuous at the top and bottom; panes contact the existing brick frame without a free edge or visible daylight seam. This elevation remains an unobserved interpretation.

The broad three-column sash meets its pale frame. Its three head slabs join the same lower-half roof layer; the upper half is external sky above that roof. The sill recess shows solid backing, with no through-hole.

verdict.bounded_verdict: Accepted for the inspected pane-to-frame contacts, concealed caps, original-texture appearance and retained silhouette. Exact archive checks establish zero roof-role or architectural physical-top changes; this is not a claim of exact photographic completion.
remaining_approximations: Only the west facade is independently photographed; north, east and south sash layouts remain provisional.
The dormer curve, pediment triangle, shutter panel divisions and sash grid are coarse at 2 blocks/metre.
Floor/threshold height, hidden west openings, chimney position, foliage and material products retain their recorded uncertainty.
Thomas retains the nearly planar 9.021-degree source facade, whose oblique raster produces half-metre steps.
